title: Beef, steak, strip, lean only eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Beef strip steak is a lean cut taken from the short loin of the cow. It contains very little fat, is rich in protein and essential micronutrients, and is commonly grilled, pan‑seared or oven‑roasted as thin slices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The strip (also called New York strip) is one of the most tender beef cuts after filet mignon.
Lean strip steaks are popular in diet plans because they provide fewer calories than fattier cuts.
Beef is a natural source of creatine, which supports muscle energy metabolism.
In the United States the strip is a staple of steak‑house menus; in Japan it is sometimes served as a lightly seared sashimi‑style steak.
Beef contains more heme iron than most plant foods, making it an excellent source of absorbable iron.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Strip steak provides about 26 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Heme iron from beef is readily absorbed, helping maintain healthy hemoglobin levels.

items.title: Source of zinc
items.content: Zinc contributes to immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: A lean strip steak contains roughly 5 g of fat per 100 g, suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef supplies vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked beef may harbor harmful bacteria (E. coli, Salmonella). Cook to an internal temperature of at least 63 °C (145 °F).

items.title: High purine content
items.content: People with gout should limit intake of purine‑rich meats.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Rare, but some individuals can be allergic to beef.

items.title: Sodium in processed cuts
items.content: If the steak is pre‑marinated, watch the added salt.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook the strip steak on high heat for 2–3 minutes per side to the desired doneness. Slice thinly against the grain for salads, sandwiches, or Asian‑style dishes such as stir‑fry or steak tataki.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh steak in the refrigerator at 0–2 °C, sealed in an airtight bag, for 3–5 days. For longer storage, freeze at –18 °C in a vacuum‑sealed package for up to 6 months. Thaw frozen steak in the fridge before cooking.
